attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation is complete only for row-normal occurrence-local functional certificates. Full EF+SAT_U remains blocked at semantic-to-occurrence extraction because SAT_U axioms can couple labels through real formula syntax and witnesses, so private occurrence-label spoofs may not preserve acceptance.
steps: Fix N, epsilon, q,rho<1+epsilon, and an accepted EF+SAT_U^{occ,rn} transcript pi claiming C(H_N^{SAT})>T_N=N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}.
Parse pi syntactically into Q_pi; for each source row x, compute the row view V_x(Q_pi) and put x in F=ForcedRows(Q_pi) iff V_x has no two compatible completions of opposite parity.
Assume |F|=E<N^{epsilon-o(1)}. For every x notin F, choose a Q_pi-compatible completion with row parity 0; for x in F, leave the real SAT occurrence labels unchanged.
By row-separability, the rowwise completions combine into one global occurrence-label assignment a' with the same Q_pi-view as the real SAT labels.
By transcript invariance, pi accepts a'. By functional label soundness, C(H_N^{a'})>T_N.
But H_N^{a'} is supported only on F, so an OR of equality tests for rows in F, with the correct hardwired output bit for each forced row, computes H_N^{a'} using O(EN) gates.
Since E<N^{epsilon-o(1)}, O(EN)=N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} below the claimed threshold after choosing the margin in T_N, contradiction.
Therefore every valid row-normal occurrence-local functional certificate must force at least N^{epsilon-o(1)} complete rows.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This proves a scoped route no-go, not P != NP. It rules out one proof-mediated beta-zero XOR certification method unless a nonrelativizing extraction theorem, sparse/nonconstructive certificate, or direct H_N lower bound is supplied.

assumptions: Circuit model is nonuniform Boolean SIZE over N-bit source inputs; equality to one exceptional row costs O(N) gates.
Psys is row-normal and occurrence-local: after parsing, every acceptance predicate factors through Q_pi and does not inspect real formula semantics except through occurrence labels.
Functional label soundness holds: if pi accepts an occurrence-label assignment a, then the induced function H_N^a has circuit size greater than T_N.
Transcript invariance is syntactic: any label assignment with the same Q_pi-view as the real SAT labels is accepted by the same transcript.
The theorem is conditional for EF+SAT_U^{occ,rn}; it does not cover full EF+SAT_U unless a semantic-to-occurrence extraction map is proved.
definitions: source object: an EF+SAT_U^{occ,rn} accepted transcript pi for the occurrence-label carrier H_N^a(x)=xor_{j<=M_N} a_{x,j}, with real labels a^{SAT}_{x,j}=SAT(G_N(x,j)).
target object: a scoped no-go/extraction theorem for proof-mediated beta-zero XOR magnification, not a proof of P != NP.
controlled interface: the parser pi -> Q_pi records row-local label atoms, row views V_x(Q_pi), and ForcedRows(Q_pi) without using the desired lower bound.
target-preserving condition: q,rho<1+epsilon, L_N=(log N)^d, beta=0, no nonuniform advice beyond pi, and substitution of SAT circuits contributes only N^{o(1)} per queried formula.
complete row: a source input x together with all M_N occurrence labels a_{x,1},...,a_{x,M_N}.
forced row: a row x for which all Q_pi-compatible completions of the occurrence labels have the same parity xor_j a_{x,j}.
private spoof A_Q: a rowwise completion of unforced rows that preserves every atom read by Q_pi while setting their row parity to a chosen easy predicate, usually 0.

ForcedRows(Q_pi) is inspectable by checking whether V_x admits two completions with opposite XOR parity; this definition is independent of C(H_N).

steps: Fix epsilon>0 and a valid length N. Work in Psys=EF+SAT_U^{occ}, where every SAT_U atom generated from G_N(x,j) is a private occurrence label unless Q_pi marks a complete row protected.

Run the parser on an accepted transcript pi to obtain Q_pi, ForcedRows(Q_pi)=F_pi, isolated point residual P_pi, and the set of occurrence labels whose values are actually inspected by the accepting computation.

Assume |F_pi|<N^{epsilon-o(1)} and |P_pi|log N<=N^{1+o(1)}. Define A_pi to agree with the transcript on inspected labels, agree with true labels on rows in F_pi, and set every other private label to the easy default D_pi.
Occurrence locality gives transcript invariance: pi sees the same labels and rule premises under A_pi, so the verifier accepts the same lower-bound certificate for H_N^{A_pi}.

Build a circuit for H_N^{A_pi}: compute D_pi and the generator bookkeeping, hardwire each forced row as an N-bit table, and patch isolated residual points. This gives C(H_N^{A_pi})<=N^{rho+o(1)}+c|F_pi|N+c'|P_pi|log N+C(D_pi).

Under rho<1+epsilon and the residual assumptions, the upper bound is <N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}, contradicting row-view soundness. Therefore any sound occurrence-local certificate must have |F_pi|>=N^{epsilon-o(1)}.

Attempted lift to full EF+SAT_U stops at EqFib(pi): private A_pi may assign different values to occurrences of the same SAT formula, so full syntax needs Realize(Q_pi,E_pi) or a large equality-fiber row charge.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a restricted route no-go conditional on the formal Psys semantics and source-threshold claim. It is not a proof of P != NP, and full EF+SAT_U remains unproved until equality fibers are either realized by the spoof or charged above the N^{epsilon-o(1)} row threshold.

assumptions: Model: EF+SAT_U^{occ} treats each generated SAT query occurrence as a private atom unless the transcript explicitly protects it; no shared formula-syntax equality is available in this restricted model.
Uniformity/cutoff: G_N is computable with overhead N^{rho+o(1)}, M_N<=N^{q+o(1)}, and all asymptotics range over valid generator lengths.
Soundness regime: an accepted transcript for a lower-bound certificate is required to be sound under every admissible occurrence-label interpretation that satisfies the same local transcript checks.
Residual regime: labels not covered by ForcedRows(Q_pi) and not in P_pi can be changed to an easy default D_pi without changing pi; |P_pi|log N<=N^{1+o(1)} in the row-view certificate model.
Threshold regime: rho<1+epsilon and C(D_pi)<=N^{1+o(1)}, so the only superlinear patch term below the claimed lower bound is |ForcedRows(Q_pi)|N.
Non-claim: this theorem audits a proof route; it does not prove C(H_N^{SAT})>N^{1+epsilon} or P != NP.
definitions: source object: Psys=EF+SAT_U^{occ} transcript pi accepted for a beta-zero XOR lower-bound certificate for H_N^{SAT}(x)=xor_{j<=M_N} SAT(G_N(x,j)), with M_N<=N^{q+o(1)} and generator overhead N^{rho+o(1)}.

target object: a route-specific no-go theorem saying that any sound occurrence-local certificate for C(H_N^{SAT})>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} must force at least N^{epsilon-o(1)} complete generator rows, unless sparse patching gives a smaller circuit.

controlled interface: parser pi -> Q_pi exposes touched private occurrence labels, complete rows, ForcedRows(Q_pi), an isolated point residual P_pi, and a perturbation A_Q acting only on unforced private labels while keeping the verifier transcript fixed.

target-preserving condition: the lower-bound implication is measured in the same nonuniform circuit model C/SIZE over the N-bit truth table of H_N^{SAT}, with no row advice and with patch circuits counted against the N^{1+epsilon} threshold.
CompleteRow(j) means the parser has a syntactic row token or protected-label set determining all N labels SAT(G_N(x,j)) for that generator row, not merely a few mentioned occurrences.
ForcedRows(Q_pi) is the set of j with CompleteRow(j) in Q_pi; this is syntactic and independent of the desired lower bound.
The spoof function H_N^A is obtained by replacing SAT labels with private Boolean labels a_{x,j} while preserving every label value read by pi and every occurrence-local rule premise.

assumptions: Full-model regime: equal SAT formulas must receive equal SAT_U labels; private occurrence perturbations that split an equality fiber are invalid.

The occurrence-local sparse spoof lifts only if there exists a row-syntax realizer A constant on every E_pi-fiber while preserving pi. Otherwise the obstruction must be charged to rows intersecting nonrealizable equality fibers.

assumptions: Constructivity regime: enumerating projected decisions and checking the cluster is polynomial in N when w+d=O(log N).
Usefulness regime: DirectClusterSound is universal over all small circuits, not merely over globally valid proof strings.
Barrier regime: if PRFs exist in SIZE(m^k) at the relevant stretch, a large constructive useful property is under standard natural-proofs pressure.

dependency_updates.description: Parser, private-label invariance, and sparse patching now form a theorem-shaped EF+SAT_U^{occ} row-charge packet with explicit threshold |F_pi|>=N^{epsilon-o(1)}.

falsifiers: Sparse-row spoof falsifier: if |ForcedRows(Q_pi)|<N^{epsilon-o(1)} and residual point cost is N^{1+o(1)}, the accepted occurrence-local transcript can certify a spoof function with a below-threshold patch circuit.

Shared-DAG equality falsifier: two occurrences of the same SAT formula in different generator rows invalidate private-label perturbations in full EF+SAT_U unless the spoof is constant on their equality fiber.
Odd-charge Tseitin falsifier: bounded local consistency can accept every local view while the global parity charge is inconsistent, so ordinary soundness is not DirectClusterSound.

Natural-property falsifier: if logarithmic projection plus DirectClusterSound is added, the route yields a valid large constructive useful property and collides with the PRF/natural-proofs pressure for the same target class.
Projection-residual falsifier: if P_pi has size N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}, the sparse patch contradiction disappears and the certificate has leaked the lower-bound-sized object into the transcript.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation is fully valid for equality-explicit EF+SAT_U, but not for unrestricted full EF+SAT_U unless every semantic use of formula identity and extension-variable reuse is extractable into Gamma_pi with a low adaptive cover or is charged as UnparsedIdentity(pi).
steps: Start with the equality-free occurrence-local theorem from cycle 83, where private labels are independent per generated SAT_U occurrence.
For full EF+SAT_U, replace independent labels by connected components of Gamma_pi, adding edges for identical formula encodings and extension-variable congruence.
Define LocSat_Gamma(Q_pi) as local proof constraints over quotient labels; this definition is syntactic and valid for equality-explicit transcripts.
Define ForcedRows_Gamma(pi) by constancy of row XOR over LocSat_Gamma; nonconstancy yields a quotient-private spoof pair preserving every quotient-local verifier check.

Assume an advice-free adaptive cover opens every quotient label touched by G_N with exponent alpha_eq. Composing G_N, the cover opener, and XOR over M_N queries gives a default circuit of size N^{max(rho,q+alpha_eq)+o(1)}.
Patch rows in ForcedRows_Gamma(pi) and residual rows R_N by equality tests on x, costing O((|ForcedRows_Gamma|+|R_N|)N^{1+o(1)})=N^{max(f,r)+1+o(1)}.
Combine the default circuit and patch circuit to obtain C(H_N^SAT)<=N^{max{rho,q+alpha_eq,max(f,r)+1}+o(1)}.
Therefore a purported certificate for C(H_N^SAT)>=N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} is refuted whenever the cap is below 1+epsilon.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a route-specific falsifier and boundary theorem. It does not prove P != NP and does not even prove the full-EF no-go until the equality-graph extraction lemma is established for the exact EF+SAT_U encoding.

assumptions: Model: nonuniform Boolean circuits measure C(.) on truth tables of length N, with H_N^SAT E-uniformly generated by G_N in overhead N^{rho+o(1)}.
Query regime: M_N<=N^{q+o(1)} and query length L_N=(log N)^d; q, rho, alpha_eq, f, r are fixed exponents up to o(1).
Proof-system regime: EF+SAT_U rules are syntactic after quotienting by Gamma_pi; no semantic formula-equivalence rule is used unless its certificate is inserted as an edge in Gamma_pi.
Binding regime: the transcript is row-parity binding outside a residual set R_N of size N^{r+o(1)} after quotienting; otherwise a private quotient-label spoof is a valid falsifier of the carrier.
Cover regime: Cover_Gamma(pi) supplies advice-free, same-length circuits for all quotient labels touched by G_N, with exponent alpha_eq and no nonuniform hard-row selector.
Non-claim: the lemma is a transfer obstruction for this carrier route only; it does not prove the main P != NP conjecture.
definitions: source object: a full EF+SAT_U proof transcript pi for the beta-zero XOR carrier H_N^SAT(x)=xor_{j<=M_N} SAT(G_N(x,j)), with real formula syntax, SAT_U oracle atoms, and extension-variable definitions.
target object: a scoped route-specific no-go theorem for proof-mediated beta-zero XOR certificates, not a proof of P != NP.

controlled interface: the parser pi -> (Q_pi,Gamma_pi,LocSat_Gamma(Q_pi),ForcedRows_Gamma(pi),Cover_Gamma(pi)) that exposes only syntactic equality, local proof constraints, quotient labels, and adaptive-cover summaries.

target-preserving condition: the quotient perturbations must respect all formula-identity and extension-congruence edges, and the derived circuit must compute the same H_N^SAT truth table in the original nonuniform circuit model.

Gamma_pi has vertices for touched SAT_U query occurrences, generated subformula occurrences, and extension-variable occurrences; edges identify syntactically identical formulas and declared extension congruences.
ForcedRows_Gamma(pi) is the set of x for which the XOR of the M_N quotient labels addressed by row x is constant over all locally satisfying quotient assignments.
alpha_eq is the adaptive-cover exponent of quotient-label opening: tau for global transcript access, a_l+mu_l for level-l summaries, and omega_l for level-l openers.

equations.label: beta_zero_xor_carrier
equations.latex: H_N^{SAT}(x)=\bigoplus_{j\le M_N} SAT(G_N(x,j)),\quad M_N\le N^{q+o(1)},\quad |G_N(x,j)|=(\log N)^d.
equations.valid_when: Valid when the beta-zero carrier family and the generator overhead are fixed uniformly before inspecting any proof transcript.

equations.label: quotient_forced_rows
equations.latex: ForcedRows_\Gamma(\pi)=\{x:\bigoplus_{j\le M_N} b_{[x,j]} \text{ is constant on } LocSat_\Gamma(Q_\pi)\}.
equations.valid_when: Valid when Gamma_pi quotients all syntactic formula identities and extension congruences appearing in the transcript.

equations.label: quotient_adaptive_cover_cap
equations.valid_when: Valid when quotient labels are opened through a declared adaptive cover with named summary and opener exponents.

equations.label: patch_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Applies after row-parity binding, quotient-cover decoding, and sparse residual patching are all preserved in the same circuit model.

equations.valid_when: Requires the target lower-bound threshold and the derived upper bound to concern the identical truth-table family H_N^SAT.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A counterexample must exhibit an EF+SAT_U rule that preserves row-parity binding by real formula semantics while producing no syntactic equality edge and no quotient adaptive cover; that would block promotion to full EF and force restriction to EF+SAT_U^{occ} or to equality-explicit EF.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Primary cycle-84 theorem packet: it upgrades the equality-free occurrence-local falsifier to a full-EF boundary theorem parameterized by the equality-quotient cover exponent.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Equality-quotient ForcedRows falsifier for full EF+SAT_U: given a full EF+SAT_U beta-zero XOR transcript pi, parse syntactic formula identity and extension-variable congruence into an equality graph Gamma_pi. If the quotient labels have adaptive cover exponent alpha_eq, the quotient-forced rows have size N^{f+o(1)}, and residual disagreement has size N^{r+o(1)}, then any row-parity-bound carrier yields C(H_N^SAT)<=N^{max{rho,q+alpha_eq,max(f,r)+1}+o(1)}. Hence a claimed N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} lower-bound certificate is invalid whenever this cap is below 1+epsilon.

assumptions: All formulas have canonical encodings or are connected by explicit equality certificates in the transcript.
Extension variables are introduced by definitional equations whose reuse creates congruence edges in Gamma_pi.
The transcript length and generated occurrence set are at most N^{O(1)} for the considered N-family.
definitions: source object: an equality-explicit EF+SAT_U transcript pi containing proof lines, SAT_U atoms, formula encodings, and extension-variable declarations.
target object: a finite quotient constraint object Q_pi/Gamma_pi used by the ForcedRows audit.
controlled interface: syntactic parsing of proof lines into local constraints and equality edges.
target-preserving condition: the parser is uniform in pi and never uses advice selecting hard rows or semantic SAT truth values.

equations.label: parser_size_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when each transcript line touches only polynomially many generated SAT_U occurrences and extension references.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Fails if the proof system permits unrecorded semantic formula equivalence as an inference rule, because Gamma_pi would then omit constraints essential to row-parity binding.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Supports the full-EF boundary by making the equality quotient syntactic and noncircular.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Parser lemma for equality-explicit EF+SAT_U: if every use of formula identity, substitution, or extension-variable congruence is syntactically recorded, then pi can be mapped to Gamma_pi and Q_pi without referencing the target lower bound or any MCSP-hard row.

assumptions: Every verifier check in EF+SAT_U^{occ} or equality-explicit EF+SAT_U reads only quotient labels and local constraints in Q_pi.
The row x is not in ForcedRows_Gamma(pi), so two satisfying quotient assignments with different row XOR exist by definition.
No external SAT oracle truth is queried beyond labels represented in the transcript object.
definitions: source object: the quotient local-satisfaction space LocSat_Gamma(Q_pi).
target object: a rule-level countermodel to row-parity binding for a nonforced row.
controlled interface: component-constant perturbations of SAT_U labels respecting Gamma_pi.
target-preserving condition: the perturbation changes only proof-internal labels and is used as a falsifier of the certificate route, not as a claim about real SAT semantics.

equations.label: nonforced_spoof_pair
equations.latex: x\notin ForcedRows_\Gamma(\pi)\Rightarrow \exists A_0,A_1\in LocSat_\Gamma(Q_\pi):\bigoplus_j A_0([x,j])\ne\bigoplus_j A_1([x,j]).
equations.valid_when: Valid when ForcedRows_Gamma is defined as constancy over the complete quotient local-satisfaction space.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Fails exactly when full EF derives a row parity from real formula identity not represented in Gamma_pi; this is the equality-graph extraction gap.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Discharges the occurrence-local invariance argument after replacing private occurrence labels by private quotient-component labels.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Quotient-private perturbation lemma: for equality-explicit EF+SAT_U, any row outside ForcedRows_Gamma(pi) admits two locally satisfying quotient assignments with opposite row parity; if the transcript claims row-parity binding for that row, this pair is a finite falsifier unless a nonlocal semantic rule is invoked.

assumptions: The desired source consequence is a lower bound C(H_N^SAT)>=N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}.
Generator and residual exponents satisfy rho<1+epsilon and r<epsilon unless explicitly declared as the escape.
The certificate route is not allowed to repair the proof by nonuniformly selecting a hard row.
definitions: source object: a candidate full-EF or MCSP/MKtP proof-mediated carrier for H_N^SAT.
target object: an escape ledger separating theorem status from unresolved full-EF extraction.
controlled interface: the exponents f, r, alpha_eq, q, rho and the presence or absence of unparsed semantic identity.
target-preserving condition: every escape must preserve advice-free row hardness in the same target circuit model.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If an example violates the disjunction while still yielding a sound full-EF row-parity certificate, then the patch upper-bound derivation has an unstated model mismatch.

candidate_lemmas.statement: Escape classification: a full-EF beta-zero certificate can evade the L84.1 falsifier only by one of three explicit mechanisms: many quotient-forced rows f>=epsilon-o(1), high quotient adaptive cover q+alpha_eq>=1+epsilon-o(1), or a nonlocal semantic identity rule not parsed into Gamma_pi.

falsifiers: A low-cover equality quotient with alpha_eq satisfying q+alpha_eq<1+epsilon and small forced/residual row exponents is a direct falsifier of the claimed beta-zero certificate.
A transcript using unrecorded semantic formula identity is a falsifier for any attempt to promote the equality-free occurrence-local theorem to full EF without an extraction lemma.
A nonuniform hard-row selector inside the MCSP/MKtP carrier invalidates the target-preserving transfer to a uniform language lower bound.
A sparse residual set R_N with |R_N|=N^{r+o(1)} and r<epsilon lets equality-test patching defeat an N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} source lower-bound claim.
A quotient opener below the adaptive-cover threshold gives small unrestricted row circuits, so local proof soundness alone is not a valid certificate of row hardness.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: For chi below the cap 1+epsilon-q, quotienting only lowers entropy and strengthens the circuit upper bound; for percolating chi near the threshold, the occurrence-local spoof stops transferring and the escape is exactly high quotient adaptive cover, not generic EF strength.
held_fixed_controls: Keep H_N^SAT, M_N<=N^{q+o(1)}, L_N=(log N)^d, and generator overhead N^{rho+o(1)} fixed.
Keep the claimed target threshold C(H_N^SAT)>=N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} fixed.
Forbid nonuniform hard-row advice and require every quotient opener to be E-uniform.
Keep residual size |R_N|<=N^{r+o(1)} and patch model unchanged.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The branch has a concrete full-EF boundary gap: does real formula identity merely create a quotient cover, or can it force row parity without becoming a small circuit? A target-preserving thought experiment isolates this parameter.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: Take a padded SAT-query family G_N where a fraction of generated queries collide syntactically across rows through shared padded cores. Build two transcripts: one equality-free EF+SAT_U^{occ} transcript and one equality-explicit EF+SAT_U transcript whose only added power is edges identifying equal padded cores.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A formal equality-graph extraction certificate: every full-EF use of formula identity must either become an edge in Gamma_pi with declared cover exponent alpha_eq, or be isolated as an UnparsedIdentity rule that blocks the full-EF promotion.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: The equality-graph component exponent chi, measured by the largest number N^{chi+o(1)} of row-query incidences opened from one quotient component, equivalently its contribution to alpha_eq.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 84 localizes the remaining full-EF obstruction: formula identity is harmless when it is parsed into a low-cover equality quotient, because the same patch upper bound follows. The only valid escape is high quotient cover, many forced rows, large residual/generator overhead, or an unparsed semantic identity rule. This converts the prior vague full-EF gap into a finite equality-graph extraction task.
